page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Don't panic!
title: Don't panic!
description:
Anna is taking the lead on the company's new stock management system. But she needs some help! She gets some advice from an unlikely member of the team. Find out what it is!
This episode focuses on politely asking for help and advice.
phrases: I would be most grateful if you could give me some help.
Please could I ask you for some advice?
I know you're busy but could you spare me a few minutes of your time please?

listening_challenge.question:
What does Denise advise Anna to do first when planning the stock management strategy?
To look at the current system.
listening_challenge.answer:
What does Denise advise Anna to do first when planning the stock management strategy?
To look at the current system.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Hello, welcome back to Tip Top Trading where everyone is gossiping about Paul’s announcement. Anna is to lead the company’s new stock management system for the new laser-curved fruit.
(Denise on phone)

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes Anna…the new girl…she’s done really well although I don’t know what experience she’s got….anyway, about the hairdresser you mentioned, oh I loved his aftershave…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I can’t understand it. I’ve got all the experience and all the ideas…she’s just such a…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom. Sorry to interrupt, I just wanted to check you’re ok with me leading this strategy for stock management.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh of course. Yeah, you deserve it.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: That was a nice touch Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But Tom, now you must help me.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Eh?!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna! That’s not the best way to ask for help. Remember what I’ve always told you about politeness?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Be polite – yes you keep telling me that.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And if you want someone to help you, ask them, don’t tell them – even if it is Tom!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. I’m in a bit of a panic. I’ve never done this before. I don’t know where to begin.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Well start by asking your colleagues for help like this:
I would be most grateful if you could give me some help
Please could I ask you for some advice?
I know you’re busy but could you spare me a few minutes of your time please?
Go on, give it a try!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right, thanks. I'll try. Erm, excuse me Tom. Sorry about earlier. I’m a little nervous about leading this strategy thing and I would be most grateful if you could give me some help… please?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Of course Anna. Why didn’t you say, I’d be delighted. I’ve lost count of the number of projects I’ve lead over the years.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Great, thanks. So… where do you think I should begin?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well, give me a few minutes and I’ll just find some of the excellent work I did last year. Basically, you’ll just need to copy it. Hold on…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah Anna… just popping out for some biscuits… err, how’s the stock management strategy coming along?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh very good Paul… actually, please could I ask you for some advice, please?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes of course… although I don’t know if I’ll be much use!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: … now where did I save those damn documents?…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I’m very grateful for this opportunity but I’m a little unsure of where to start. Tom is looking for some his old work but…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Really?! To be honest, this isn’t Tom’s speciality. At a time like this I would ask Denise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Denise!?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes… she may only be the office assistant but she always has words of wisdom. Right… custard creams or chocolate digestives?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Biscuits?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh… custard creams please. Err, Denise, I know you’re busy but could you spare a few minutes of your time please?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Of course Anna, always happy to help you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well you know the stock management control system?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: The one you’ve now got to work out… well done for getting that!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. I really don’t know where to begin. It was OK writing it down for Paul but how do I put it in to practice? There’s just too much to do!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Calm down Anna. You’ll be fine. The first thing you need to do is to look at our current system.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Look at our current system. How do I do that?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Easy! Just take the lift down to the warehouse and speak to Mr Ingle and then write down what you find – and draw up an action plan of tasks you need to do – like a shopping list – I’m very good at those.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Go and see Mr Ingle? Oh do I have to.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: He’s ok really Anna. If you approach him in the right way he won’t bite your head off!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What? Bite my head off! Oh… well, if he won’t bite me… then I suppose I should go and see him. Thanks for your advice Denise, I could kiss you. Right, I’m going to go and see him right now.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Make an action plan! A good idea. Well done Denise, you’re smarter than you look! And well done Anna, you eventually got the help you needed by using these phrases:

I would be most grateful if you could give me some help
Please could I ask you for some advice?
I know you’re busy but could you spare me a few minutes of your time please?
Remember, if you’re stuck for ideas just ask for help…but maybe not Tom, I wonder how he’s getting on?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: (shouting across room) Here Anna, I’ve got them. Look, all my ideas from my last stock control project…pages and pages of them. Just copy these, they’re brilliant. Anna? Anna!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: …too late, I’ve just seen her in the lift. Fancy a custard cream Tom?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So Anna is off to speak to the prickly Mr Ingle. Let’s hope she uses those phrases to ask for help, otherwise she might get her head bitten off – and it could get very messy! See you next time.
